findings.title: Above rear_warning_size 1.35 the heavy burst is no larger than a grunt's, and the size slider does nothing
findings.detail: SPEC §8 says the Bruiser and boss get a larger burst, and SPEC §11 makes burst size a tuning slider. RearWarning._steady_size() multiplies base_px x size x heavy_scale and then clamps to the corner's short side (216 px at 1080p). So once base x size reaches 216/1.3 = 166 px (size 1.04), the heavy burst stops growing and the grunt burst catches up. Ratios: 1.30 at size 1.0, 1.23 at 1.1, 1.12 at 1.2, and 1.00 from 1.35 up to the slider's 3.0. From 1.35 to 3.0 (about 60% of the range above the default) neither burst changes size and heavies look like grunts. At the default, the first frames of the heavy pop are also clipped: 216 px against the grunt's 200, a ratio of 1.08. The instruments cannot catch this: the oracle and probe check the heavy flag, not the drawn size; headless runs use a square 1920x1920 viewport that never hits the 216 px clamp; and test_ui only checks that every size stays inside the corner.
findings.evidence: captures/review/probe2b.log (1920x1080 control). Heavy against grunt: size 1.00 gives 208/160 px; 1.10 gives 216/176; 1.20 gives 216/192; 1.35, 1.50, 2.00 and 3.00 all give 216/216. Sheet captures/review/size15/sheets/size_compare.png: top row size 1.0 (the heavy burst on the right is larger), bottom row 'Warn: heavy' recorded with --tune=rear_warning_size=1.5 (both bursts the same size). Code: game/ui/rear_warning.gd:314-320 (_steady_size clamp), 148-155 (burst_rect clamp); game/autoload/tuning_data.gd:815 (size range 0.25-3.0), 829 (heavy_scale).
findings.repro: In F1, set Rear warning > rear_warning_size to 1.5. Let a Bruiser (or the boss) and a Punk wind up behind-left and behind-right; both corner bursts are 216 px. Headless: run tests/test_zz_review_warn2.gd::test_heavy_burst_against_size in the review worktree.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the ratio inside the clamp: cap the grunt size at edge / rear_warning_heavy_scale and draw a heavy burst at grunt x heavy_scale, so a heavy is always heavy_scale times larger and fits the corner. Alternatively, limit the slider to what fits, about 1.04 at the defaults. Add a test_ui assertion that heavy is larger than grunt at every size on a 16:9 canvas.

findings.title: During the back elbow's 150-degree view turn, a wind-up ahead of the look is unseen and unwarned
findings.detail: SPEC §8 fires the warning for an enemy 'more than 55° from camera forward'. The build measures from look_yaw (decided call, M3-judgement-calls.md line 33, whose reasoning names spins and the KO view). The back elbow (RB, M2) is different: it turns the first-person view 150 degrees over the shoulder (camera_yaw_deg -150, held 6 frames) without changing look_yaw. For 19 of its 26 frames the camera points more than 55 degrees off the look. In that window, a Punk dead ahead of the look that starts its jab is 150 degrees off camera forward: off screen and unwarned. The probe shows it unwarned for its whole 22-frame wind-up (lit=false every frame) and off camera for the first 16 of those frames (cam-bearing 150 down to 56), visible only from 39 degrees, 5 frames before the strike. The reverse also happens: an enemy behind the look that winds up during the elbow lights the corners while it is plainly on screen. With the director favouring out-of-view (by look) enemies and a wind-up gap of 21 frames, a wind-up in that window is not rare in a crowd. The departure from the spec text is not in 'Possible spec departures (for Game-boy's ruling)', while the other warning departures (fixed side, 46-55 degree band, reach includes travel) are.
findings.evidence: captures/review/probe2.log. 'back elbow view yaw per frame: 0:-16 1:-53 2:-97 3:-134 4..13:-150 14:-147 ... 20:-56 21:-39 ... frames with |view| > 55: 19'. 'punk ahead during back elbow: 0:WU cam-bearing 150 lit=false ... 16:WU cam-bearing 56 lit=false | 17:WU cam-bearing 39 lit=false ... 21:WU cam-bearing 0 lit=false | 22:AT'. Code: tools/gen_moves.gd:72-74, 190-195 (BACK_ELBOW_VIEW_YAW_DEG -150, hold 6); game/player/player.gd:956-989 (_update_view_yaw); game/camera/first_person_camera.gd:261-262 (view = view_yaw x look basis); game/ui/rear_warning.gd:259-267 (bearing from look_bearing_deg only).
findings.repro: Crowd room, AI frozen: place a Punk 1.0 m dead ahead, press RB (back elbow), then force_attack(0) on the Punk 4 frames later. No corner lights, and the Punk is off screen for 16 of its 22 wind-up frames. Headless: tests/test_zz_review_warn2.gd::test_back_elbow_view_turn.
findings.suggested_fix: Either record it for Game-boy's ruling in M3-judgement-calls.md 'Possible spec departures' (the warning reads the look, not the camera; the back elbow's view turn is the visible case), or have the HUD widget, which is presentation and may read the view, also light a corner for an attacker more than rear_warning_angle_deg off the look rotated by player.get_camera_view_yaw(), while the director and the oracle stay on the look. Prefer the doc entry unless Game-boy wants the camera reading.

I reviewed the merged M3 build at 7a015cc through the L2 crowd lens, in worktree /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m3-review-final-crowd. I used P4-int's recordings and twelve runs of my own: seven Movie Maker recordings (knockdown lens, line-up, mixed waves, boss wave, guard vs wind-up) and headless fixed-fps runs with a pop monitor, a lens-cover sampler and the engage meter. My probe acts are in tests/bot/acts/zz_review_acts.gd, untracked and not committed. No Godot process is left running.

**Hard metrics:** R1, R2, R3, R10 and R11 pass in every act and seed I ran, and tools/check_m3_log.py says ok on every log.

**Four real defects:**
1. **High.** Every knockdown from the side or behind puts the first-person lens 4.4 cm under the street for about 1.1 s. The floor vanishes and the player sees the undersides of the level. This is what P4-int called the "pale floor slab"; it is not the player's own body. In a crowd it is the usual case: all four knockdowns of a passive mixed crowd came from outside the view.
2. **Medium.** The APPROACH state takes the straight navmesh path through the player to a slot on his far side. Avoidance turns this into an orbit at 0.75-0.9 m, facing him. A purple Bruiser filled the view for 3.5 s while it was not attacking. This is the main cause of the R8 lens-cover misses in the mixed fight.
3. **Medium.** The Kicker's blind-side ring rotation keeps the whole fought crowd walking between slots. On average only 0.4-0.8 of 5.8 enemies are posturing; the same six with the rotation off posture 1.7-2.0, as six Punks do (1.7). This breaks SPEC §7 ("most of their time posturing") and the posture share the slice gate accepted.
4. **Low.** The evidence pack and the waves test never reach a mixed wave. "Waves to the boss" plays two Punk-only waves and a boss that throws one wind-up. My own runs fill the gap, and the mixed waves pass.

**Two low flags:**
- The face-up "belly slab" covers 71-77% of the lens for about 1 s. This is Game-boy's call.
- A bruised Kicker drifts toward the clean Thug's colour.

**What passes:** the posture ring, guards that never look like wind-ups, attackers backing off, armor hits that register, flinch-lock, get-up pops (none in 9 runs), the Kicker's flank, archetype identity when clean, and the boss in the street.

The Kicker's jump kick travels 0.27 m per frame (about 16 m/s) over its 6 active frames. Whether it reads is for L3.

findings.title: Face-down knockdowns (hit from the side or behind) put the first-person lens 4.4 cm under the street: the floor vanishes for about 1.1 s
findings.detail: In a non-KO knockdown the lens rides EyePoint plus cam_height_offset_m (-0.2 m), with no floor clamp; the KO view applies only when health <= 0. When the player falls face-down, EyePoint lies 0.15-0.18 m above the floor, so the lens sits at -0.044 m, inside the 1 m floor box. The floor is culled from below, and the lower 60% of the view becomes the background colour, with the undersides of curbs, doorstep boxes and the alley floor hanging under a horizon line. This lasts the whole DOWNED time: 67-68 frames (1.1 s) per knockdown. Face-up knockdowns, from the front, keep the lens at 0.116 m (finding 5). In a crowd the face-down case is the usual one: blind-spot priority sends the Kicker, the main knockdown source, from outside the view 60-90% of the time. In 'Review: mixed passive' all 4 knockdown hits came from outside the view: a sweep warned on both corners, a sweep on the right, and two Bruiser smashes on the left. P4-int's own observed recording shows it, and P4-int.md:70 misread it as the player's own body. A player would see the street disappear every time he is swept from behind; with the belly slab, every knockdown blinds him for 1-1.1 s.

findings.title: APPROACH takes the straight path through the player to a far-side slot: non-attacking enemies orbit at 0.75-0.9 m facing him and wall 51-80% of the lens, for up to 3.5 s
findings.detail: _tick_approach walks the navmesh path to its posture slot and faces the player while within the ring. The navmesh doesn't know the player; he is only a 0.3 m avoidance obstacle. So an enemy that is inside the ring, after a reaction or while entering, with its slot on his far side, walks straight at him. Avoidance then slides it round his nose at contact distance, guard up, facing him, and sometimes it stands still there (v = 0 for 0.5 s at 0.81 m). In the mixed fight a Bruiser, after a break-free, spent f883-f1090 (3.5 s) at 0.80-0.98 m in APPROACH, with its slot -105 to -58 degrees round, covering 51-71% of the lens. In the frames its purple chest and arms fill about 90% of the view, face out of the top. A boss add did the same on entry after two jabs: f835-f890, slot 152 to 57 degrees round, 62-80% cover, while a rear warning lit behind it. findings.title: The Kicker's blind-side ring rotation keeps a fought mixed crowd walking: posture falls to 0.4-0.8 of 5.8 enemies (1.7-2.0 without it)
findings.detail: With a Kicker alive, every reslot (every 1.5 s, on a spawn or death, or when the player moves 1 m) turns the whole ring so that a slot sits behind the look, and the Kickers take the rearmost slots first, bumping their occupants. In a fight the player keeps turning, so 'behind' keeps moving and the other five keep being sent to new slots, often across the player, which feeds finding 2. Same six, same seeds, prefers_blind_side switched off: POSTURE averages 1.66-1.98 against 0.38-0.78 with the rotation, and APPROACH 1.46-1.56 against 2.87-3.12. Lens-over-half samples are 5.7-8.2% against 9.8-14.9% (APPROACH-caused: 3-4 against 12-34), and the widest empty arc averages 119-127 against 133-148 degrees. Six Punks fought posture 1.7 on average, so the mixed crowd without the rotation matches the slice, and the rotation alone cuts posturing by 55-80%. The P2-kicker call costed this as 'pulling the others by up to half a step'; measured, it breaks SPEC §7 ('spend most of their time posturing') and the accepted 'a third to two fifths of the time'. A fought mixed crowd postures 7-13% of the time. The Kicker's flank is worth keeping (blind-side share 60-90%); the side effect on the others is the defect.

tells.summary:
Lens L3 (archetype tells and identity), final M3 review at 7a015cc, in the worktree /Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m3-review-final-tells. I recorded every enemy attack with force_attack on a frozen AI, at 3 m and at its own strike range (reach_m - engage_margin_m). I also recorded taunts with posture_taunt_chance 1.0, the armor, haymaker and mash-free acts, the Thug drop and pickup acts, and boss phase 2. Each recording was measured headless with a lens probe I wrote. It logs the nearest enemy mesh to the real camera each frame and the share of the view covered.

The tells mostly hold. Every attack reads as itself from 3 m, and the wind-ups differ within each archetype:
- Punk: cocked fist for the jab, raised open palms for the shove.
- Kicker: frontal crouch for the jump kick, side-on drop for the sweep.
- Thug: pipe raised high and held.
- Bruiser: both arms up for the smash, arms out horizontally for the grab.
- Boss: crouch for the charge, Y-arms for the pound, arms wide for the grab.

Armor reads (grey spark, no flinch, the wind-up runs on), the haymaker's break works, and the grab, MASH prompt, break-free and headbutt work.

Five defects survived checking:
1. The boss's ground pound folds its body over and drives its cap through the lens whenever the player stands within about 1.2 m, which is where he punches it from. In a real autopilot fight the cap comes within 0.03 m and fills 100% of the view.
2. The Thug's dropped pipe never comes to rest. It rolls toward and past the player, leaves LB's reach after 2.8 s and is 4.5 m away after 18 s, still rolling.
3. The Thug's taunt raises its pipe above its head for a second. This is the shared open-handed taunt with the pipe in the hand, and it reads as its pipe wind-up.
4. The boss's grab slam reads as the Bruiser's headbutt from the lens: its cap dives into the view (0.115 m while the player is still held).
5. Phase 2's beckon is cut one frame after it starts, because the adds' arrival re-seats the boss. The boss then walks past the player's shoulder (0.85 m, 59% of the view) to its new seat on the far side.

The targeted tests are green (test_boss 39/39, test_pipe_thug 19/19, test_player_grabbed 15/15, test_enemy_moves_punk 9/9, test_bruiser 27/27). None of them covers these cases. The temporary review acts are in tests/bot/acts/zz_review_acts.gd in the worktree, not committed.

findings.title: The Thug's dropped pipe never comes to rest: it rolls past the player and out of LB's reach within 3 s
findings.detail: Weapon.drop() hands the capsule rigid body a 0.5 m/s push toward the hitter plus a spin about the vertical. On the floor the capsule turns that push into rolling, which nothing stops: there is no rolling resistance, and only the default angular damping slowly cuts it down. The pipe lands 0.57 m from the player, then rolls under and past him at about 0.45 m/s. The collision mask is world-only, so it passes through his body. It leaves pickup_range (1.5 m) 2.8 s after landing, and 18 s later it is still rolling 4.5 m away. The LB PICK UP cue goes out while the player has done nothing. A player who looks down sees the prize roll away behind him, and in a crowd he rarely gets to LB within 3 s. This breaks the P2-thug acceptance ('the pipe lies where it can be reached') and P2-thug call 1's measured rest of 0.64-1.03 m in front of him. test_pipe_thug only checks the pipe after 90 ticks (SETTLE_TICKS), while it is still in reach.
findings.evidence: captures/review/pipe_headless2.log (act 'RV pipe watch' wrapping ThugActs._drops): 'RVPIPE f141 cue on ... pipe d 0.57 avail true vel 1.76', 'f291 cue on pipe d 1.40 vel 0.40', 'f307 cue off ... pipe d 1.50 vel 0.39', 'f611 ... d 2.99 vel 0.23', 'f1211 ... d 4.46 vel 0.09'. Recording captures/review/thugboss/bot.avi, sheet sheets/thug_drop.png: the cue is shown in frames 8-17 and gone in frames 18-20 with the player still. The same in P4-int's pickup.png frame 14. Code at game/weapons/weapon.gd:100-114 (drop) and :121-126 (_set_ground_physics: no damping or physics material). tests/test_pipe_thug.gd:16 SETTLE_TICKS 90.
findings.repro: Record 'Thug drops the pipe' and keep watching the street after the knockdown for 5 s. Or run the review act 'RV pipe watch' headless and grep RVPIPE. In game: knock a Thug down with P P P P, wait 3 s, press LB: nothing is picked up.
findings.suggested_fix: Make a dropped pipe settle. Options: lock its rotation except yaw while it lies on the ground; give it high angular and linear damping once it touches the floor, or let it sleep after settling; or a physics material with rolling friction. Whichever is used, any value goes in TuningData (Pipe Thug subgroup), not a script constant. Add a test that the pipe is still within pickup_range 5 s after the drop.

findings.title: The Pipe Thug's taunt raises its pipe above its head, and it reads as the pipe wind-up

It turns both hands palm-up with the arms out, and it is tested only for a Punk's hands below the shoulders. The Thug keeps its pipe in the right hand through it. findings.title: The boss's grab slam reads as the Bruiser's headbutt from the lens: the cap dives into the view while the player is still held
findings.detail: The slam's strike pose bends the boss forward over the player ('throws him down and forward over its bent body', grab_poses.gd _slam). EnemyHold lets the player go and applies the THROWN hit by code at the strike frame. So nothing on screen throws him: the boss's forward fold just drives its head through where his face is. From first person, the last fifth of the slam's wind-up is the cap filling the screen, then BOFF and a knockback. That is the same picture as the Bruiser's headbutt (the grey cap into the face, THUD). The cap is 0.115 m from the lens at boss_slam f53, one frame before the strike, while the player is still GRABBED. The lift before it is only a small rise of the view. L3 asks each attack to read as itself. The boss's signature 25-damage attack and the Bruiser's headbutt are not told apart, and the 0.25 m held-view rule is broken before any hit lands. test_player_grabbed judges the hold only up to 80% of the follow-up's wind-up, which is exactly where the dive begins.
findings.evidence: captures/review/tells_headless.log: 'RVL Boss grab 1.25 m: nearest enemy mesh to the lens 0.115 m at f3338 (Cap, boss_slam f53, player GRABBED)'. Recording captures/review/tells/bot.avi t=55.3-55.9 s (tells/frames/slam_end.png: the orange cap grows to fill the view in frames 6-10, then BOFF) against t=42.7-43.3 s (tells/frames/headbutt_end.png: the grey cap into the view, THUD). The test window is at tests/test_player_grabbed.gd:226-230 (roundi(follow.startup * WINDUP_HOLD_AT)).
findings.repro: Record 'Boss grab slam' (or 'RV tells strike', the last attack) and view the 0.5 s before the throw. Then compare with 'Bruiser headbutt'.
findings.suggested_fix: Author the slam's strike so the boss's head stays back and the arms carry the motion. For example, the torso turns and both arms swing the held player up and down to one side, so the victim's view lurches up and sideways before the release. Or release at the top of the lift with an up-and-back THROWN knockback. Extend the held-view clearance check to the whole follow-up up to its strike frame for the slam (keep the headbutt's deliberate dive exempt).

findings.title: The phase 2 beckon is cut one frame after it starts, and the boss then walks past the player's shoulder to a new seat
findings.detail: _enter_phase2() starts the beckon (_start_taunt) and calls in the first Punk on the same tick. On the director's next update the set of enemies has changed, so _assign_slots() re-spreads the ring. The new Punks sit where they spawn, and the greedy match can hand the boss the seat across the player. The boss is now off its slot, so _tick_posture() sends it to APPROACH, and _enter_approach() zeroes _taunt_frames. The beckon is gone after one frame. The boss then walks in a straight line from in front of the player to behind him, passing 0.85 m from him at bearing -23 with its body covering 59% of the view. A 2.3 m boss marching at arm's length without attacking reads like a charge. So the phase change Game-boy sees is the bar halving and the boss walking straight at him, not 'the turn, the beckon, the adds walking in'. In three autopilot fights the beckon started only once: in the other two the boss was in APPROACH or LAUNCHED at the change, so it was never started. The Kicker's orbit (kicker.gd _posture_target) solves the same straight-through walk for the Kicker only.
findings.evidence: captures/review/phase2_headless.log ('RV lens: Boss phase 2' wrapping BossActs._phase2): 'RVPHASE f16779 phase 2: boss state FREE ai POSTURE ... taunt_frames 66', 'RVBOSS f16780 APPROACH dist 4.03 bearing 0 slot (-1.351567, 0.2, 5.187556) taunt 0' (the slot is behind the player), 'RVBOSS nearest during the phase 2 APPROACH: 0.85 m at f16911 bearing -23', 'RVLENS Boss phase 2: ... max cover 59% at f16888 (RightForearm of Boss1, - f70, enemy FREE)'. Autopilot fights: 'RVPHASE no beckon within 2 s of the change' (seed 0, APPROACH) and 'boss state LAUNCHED' (seed 2). Recording captures/review/thugboss/bot.avi: sheets/phase2_change.png (frame 4 is the bar halving, then the boss walks toward the lens in guard) and sheets/phase2_after.png frames 1-4 (the boss's body sweeps past filling half the view). Code: boss.gd:258-266, enemy_actor.gd:476-484 and :531-538, enemy_director.gd:443-500.
findings.repro: Record 'Boss phase 2 adds' and view t=6.9-10 s. Or run the review act 'RV lens: Boss phase 2' headless and grep RVBOSS/RVPHASE.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the beckon finish before the boss leaves its seat: in Boss, hold the posture (ignore 'strayed') while the taunt plays. Or skip the boss in the reslot that the call-in's spawns trigger (keep its claim). Route any reslot walk round the ring instead of through the player, generalising the Kicker's orbit into the base or the director. Add a test: at phase 2 from POSTURE, the taunt clip plays for its full length and the boss's flat distance to the player stays at least posture_ring_min_m - 0.5 during the following APPROACH.

findings.title: Knees on a Bruiser the player holds are absorbed as armor: a grey spark, a clank, ARMOR in the log, and no held jolt
findings.detail: The player can grab a Bruiser only when it is staggered (or its armor is broken), and the knee is the grab's payoff. EnemyActor._apply_armor (enemy_actor.gd:815-831) applies armor_light whatever the victim's state, including GRABBED. CombatActor.receive_hit then returns at combat_actor.gd:424-428, before _apply_reaction's held-victim jolt (combat_actor.gd:1041). Every knee on a held, staggered Bruiser therefore shows the armor feedback: a grey spark and no reaction of the held body, unlike every other held enemy. Nobody decided this interaction: the armor calls are about the Bruiser's own wind-ups and standing hits. In first person it reads as 'my knee bounced off' at the moment the stagger-then-grab counter is meant to pay off.
findings.evidence: Probe test_review_knees_on_a_held_bruiser (captures/review/probe4.log) prints 'hit knee on Bruiser1: tier 0 armor_absorbed true reaction 0, victim state 10 anim held'. In the first-person sheet captures/review/bruiser_grab/knee_sheet.png (act 'Grab the staggered Bruiser', bot.log f112 'Knee 6.0 dmg LIGHT'), frames 5-6 (row 1 col 5, row 2 col 1) show a grey star spark on the held Bruiser and no burst or word. Frames 6-10 show the same held pose (no jolt). Compare the throw in row 3 (THUD and a red burst).
findings.repro: tools/capture_bot.sh res://tests/bot/crowd_bot.tscn captures/review/bruiser_grab "Grab the staggered Bruiser". Then: ffmpeg -ss 1.55 -t 1.67 -i bot.avi -vf fps=12,scale=480:-1,tile=5x4 -frames:v 1 knee_sheet.png. Or in play: hook a Bruiser, LB, P.
findings.suggested_fix: In EnemyActor._apply_armor, return early while state == GRABBED and hit.attacker == holder, so the hold's own knees jolt as on any held body. Alternatively, log it as a default for Game-boy's ruling and leave it.

findings.title: The boss's phase-2 call-in spawns Punks while F1 or F4 is open, which A2.2's fight hold forbids
findings.detail: A2.2 says that while GameInput.menu_open is true the fight holds and waves start no spawns. The wave loop honours this (encounter_spawner.gd:214), but the boss's call-in does not. Boss._tick_adds (boss.gd:237-254) keeps counting down _adds_frames and calls spawner.spawn_adds() (encounter_spawner.gd:122), and neither checks menu_open. The adds come 0.6 s apart (wave_spawn_interval_s). If Game-boy opens F1 just after the hit that halves the boss, the second Punk walks in while the panel is open. Editing boss_phase2_at or boss_adds_count live in F1 spawns them with the panel open. The spawned Punks stand still while the menu is open, so no damage follows; the violation is that the hold is not total.
findings.evidence: Probe test_review_boss_adds_while_a_menu_is_open (captures/review/probe2.log): with GameInput.menu_open = true and boss_phase2_at set to 0.95 on a boss at 90% health, it printed 'boss phase 2, alive before 1, alive after 3 with the menu open, adds 2'. The assertion 'nothing spawns while a menu is open (A2.2)' failed: expected 1, got 3.
findings.repro: In the crowd room, F4-spawn the boss, bring it to just above 50%, land the halving hit and press F1 within 0.6 s. Or open F1 and drag boss_phase2_at above the boss's health share. Headless: tools/run_tests.sh -gselect=test_zz_review_probe -gunit_test_name=test_review_boss_adds_while_a_menu_is_open (temporary probe in the review worktree).
findings.suggested_fix: In Boss._tick_adds, return before the countdown while GameInput.menu_open, as the spawner's _physics_process does. Optionally do the same for Tuning.data.ai_frozen. Phase 2 itself can still trigger; only the spawns wait.

findings.title: Archetypes override ten base-private members outside the documented hook list, and two overrides are guarded by no test
findings.detail: EnemyActor's contract (enemy_actor.gd:35-37) says archetypes override only the listed hooks, 'never the control tick'. The code does more. boss.gd overrides _tick_control (217), _face (171) and react_to_block (195). react_to_block re-implements CombatActor's recoil branch (combat_actor.gd:398-405) and writes its private _recoiling, so any change to the base recoil silently diverges. bruiser.gd overrides _tick_control (140), _stop (158), _animate_legs (167) and CombatActor._pin_spot (127). kicker.gd overrides _posture_target (75), _enter_posture (87) and _pick_strafe_dir (137). Its _enter_posture relies on a same-physics-frame handshake (Engine.get_physics_frames()) with the base's _tick_approach and _tick_recover call order, and it writes the base's _progress_best and _progress_frames. pipe_thug.gd rewrites _attacks and _next_attack (110-111). Disabling each override one at a time fails at least one test in nine of the eleven cases. Removing kicker _pick_strafe_dir fails none of test_kicker.gd's 16 tests, because test_a_kicker_that_is_in_view_strafes_toward_the_edge_of_the_view passes on the base's slot-seeking direction. Removing bruiser _animate_legs fails none of test_bruiser.gd's 27 tests: the brace test only covers _stop.
findings.evidence: Mutation runs (rename the override, run its test file, git checkout). Kicker: _enter_posture 13/16 pass, _posture_target 13/16, _pick_strafe_dir 16/16. Boss: _face 38/39, react_to_block 37/39, _tick_control 29/39. Bruiser: _stop 26/27, _animate_legs 27/27, _pin_spot 26/27, _tick_control 24/27. PipeThug: _on_hit_received 12/19.

findings.suggested_fix: Promote the real extension points to documented hooks, for example a turn-rate scale for _face, a post-tick hook instead of _tick_control, a CombatActor _recoil(frames) helper that both the base and the boss call, a strafe-direction hint, and a 'legs locked' query. Add a test where the Kicker's strafe direction differs from the slot-seeking one (no slot, or slot on the far side). Add a test that a strafing, braced Bruiser keeps its brace clip.

findings.title: Tests write fixed user:// files shared by every worktree: a flake risk when suites run in parallel
findings.detail: Every worktree is the same Godot project ('Beat-em-Up PoC'), so all of them share one user:// directory. CLAUDE.md's parallel-worktree pattern runs several suites at once. test_check_m3_log.gd:26 writes user://check_m3_log_test.log, then runs python3 on it, about 8 times. test_readability_probe.gd:916 uses user://probe_test, and test_readability_probe.gd:938 deletes, expects and reads back user://readability.json, the same path the bot probe falls back to (readability_probe.gd:310). Two suites in two worktrees can overwrite or delete each other's file between the write and the read. test_tuning_panel.gd:6-21 already documents this hazard and scopes its directory with OS.get_process_id().
findings.evidence: ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/Beat-em-Up PoC/ holds check_m3_log_test.log and readability.json, written by these tests, beside gut_tuning_3920 (the PID-scoped one). The code is at test_check_m3_log.gd:26 and test_readability_probe.gd:916, :938.
findings.repro: Run tools/run_tests.sh -gselect=test_check_m3_log in two worktrees at the same moment. One run can parse the other's log text, or find readability.json deleted.
findings.suggested_fix: Suffix the paths with OS.get_process_id(), as test_tuning_panel.gd does. Make test_write_on_exit point the probe at a per-PID folder instead of the user:// root.

findings.title: The probe's lens-coverage sampling is keyed to the absolute frame counter, so R8 drifts between identical runs
findings.detail: readability_probe.gd:355 samples the lens when Engine.get_physics_frames() % lens_every == 0. Which frames get sampled therefore depends on how many frames earlier tests or acts ran. In the two full-suite runs, a 6-frame shift (caused by the pipe test's physics-dependent wait) changed test_slice_crowd's 'six punks, still player' R8 p95 from 33% to 35% with identical game behaviour. R8 is soft and is quoted in the gate files with its p95. The same act can report a different number run to run, which weakens 'measured in every seed' claims.
findings.evidence: Diff of captures/review/tests_run1.log and tests_run2.log, cleaned of colour codes (r1.txt and r2.txt in captures/review): line 1159 'R8 lens covered by enemies p50 5%, p95 33%' vs 'p95 35%'. WARN-CHECK frames are shifted by exactly 6 (f68177 vs f68171). The earlier difference is 'the dropped pipe lies 1.01 m' vs '0.97 m' (test_pipe_thug.gd:422).
findings.repro: Run tools/run_tests.sh twice and diff the READABILITY blocks of 'six punks, still player'.
findings.suggested_fix: Sample on (frame - _start_frame) % lens_every, and the same for occlusion_every, so the cadence is relative to the act's start.

fair.summary:
Lens L5 (fairness and pacing) at 7a015cc. Method: 75 probed acts, all at real damage (none in god mode), over 3 seeds, plus 4 first-person recordings. Players modelled: passive; the held-back autopilot; the full autopilot; a "masher" (full autopilot, no block or dodge); and a slower human (20-frame reaction, 270 deg/s turn). Fights covered: the mixed six with top-ups, 1 to 6 Punks, heavies, Thugs, 6 min and 3 min of waves, and the boss alone and as its wave.

The hard metrics pass everywhere:
- R1: max 2.
- R2: min 21 f.
- R3: 0 unwarned of 1370 hits on the player.
- R11: max 15 over 111 non-boss knockdowns.
- R10: 100% wherever printed.
- The full suite passes, 1130/1130, with no SCRIPT ERROR or ERROR.
- No flinch-lock: the longest reaction chain in any act is one knockdown (2.30 s max), and no other attacker lands a hit within 150 f of a knockdown.
- A passive player is KO'd in 15.4-25.8 s by the mixed six (R12 holds; worst 2 s is 30-32).
- Waves repeat with no leaks: 20 waves and 4 boss waves in 6 min, node count back to about 4600 at every clear, 0 orphans.

What fails is pacing. The danger falls away as soon as the player attacks:
1. HIGH. The boss can be stun-locked to death. After every knockdown it walks back to its ring slot (APPROACH), and in APPROACH it never asks for a token. Each P P P P or K K K chain carries a heavy hit that staggers it and a finisher that floors it. The full autopilot kills it in 38-40 s while it throws 1-2 attacks. With boss_health 600 and cooldown 0.5 s it still throws nothing after its opener. The knobs the README names cannot fix this.
2. MEDIUM. The same root cause applies to the whole crowd. 42% of the 234 enemies killed by aggressive players never wound up once, including 12 of 34 Bruisers. A masher with no defence takes less damage per minute than a defensive player.
3. MEDIUM. The F1 attacker_cap slider does nothing from 2 to 6: the director's line rule lets only one attacker step in at a time. Damage also stops rising past 4 enemies.
4. LOW-MEDIUM. An armoured Bruiser in APPROACH can jam against the player and fill the lens for about 3-5 s. It neither moves nor attacks, and jabs are absorbed, so nothing knocks it out of that state (R13 miss, 3 events in one run).
5. LOW. tools/check_m3_log.py falsely FAILs a multi-act log when a wind-up starts between acts.

R12's Thug case is fair. The chain needs a landed or blocked swing, and there is a gap to guard after the first swing's flinch; the autopilot parried swing 2 or 3 more than once. A reacting player takes 10-20, not 30.

findings.title: The boss can be stun-locked to death: after every knockdown it walks back to its slot and never gets to attack
findings.detail: In APPROACH an enemy never asks for a token: wants_token() needs ai_state POSTURE (enemy_actor.gd:197-202). Every reaction ends in _enter_approach() (enemy_actor.gd:449), and the enemy then walks to its ring slot 2.5-4 m away (_tick_approach, enemy_actor.gd:487-495). So a boss that gets up beside the player turns to walk away. The boss's armor absorbs heavy hits only while it winds up or runs a charge or pound (boss.gd:148-161), never while walking. So the standard chains loop on it. P P P P: jab and jab are absorbed (grey spark), the hook staggers it, the uppercut floors it. K K K: the front kick is absorbed, the roundhouse staggers, the spinning heel floors it. It gets up, walks (APPROACH), and the next chain lands before it reaches POSTURE. The full autopilot kills the 300 HP, two-phase boss in 38-40 s (3 seeds), and the boss lands 1-2 attacks (one charge or pound, 15-21 damage in all). In seed 0 the boss spends 12% of the run in REACT, 7% in APPROACH and 1% in POSTURE; it is KO'd at f2411. P3-boss, P4-int (call 12) and the README put this down to boss_health and boss_attack_cooldown_s. Those knobs do not reach it. With boss_attack_cooldown_s 0.5 and boss_health 600 it still throws nothing after its opener: 19 REACT->APPROACH->REACT cycles, 0% POSTURE, killed at 67 s (boss_knobs.log). In first person Game-boy sees the boss fall, rise, turn and fall again, every 5 s, with the boss bar draining and his own HP still at 85/100.

findings.title: A 6-enemy fight barely threatens a player who attacks: chased enemies never fight back, and 42% of the killed never wind up
findings.detail: This shares finding 1's root cause: a hit sends an enemy to APPROACH, and in APPROACH or ENTER it cannot get a token. A player who walks up and punches keeps whoever he is hitting in REACT/APPROACH, and only enemies sitting in POSTURE on the ring ever attack him. Against a mixed six refilled whenever one falls, over 3 seeds and 60 s each: (a) The full autopilot takes 14-24 damage a minute (5-7 hits) and kills 27-29. (b) A masher, the full autopilot with defend off (no block, no dodge), takes 44-80 a minute and kills 26-29, never KO'd. That is less than the defensive slow held-back player, who takes 83-126 a minute and is KO'd once in seed 2. (c) The crowd winds up 13-21 times a minute against aggressive players and 34-46 against held-back ones. (d) Of 234 enemies the aggressive players killed, 98 (42%) never wound up once: 33 of 79 Punks, 38 of 82 Kickers, 15 of 39 Thugs, 12 of 34 Bruisers. (e) Bruisers last about 4.5 s once touched; Bruiser1 in fight_s0 was hit first at f4721 and KO'd at f4992, still in APPROACH. (f) In 6 min of waves the full autopilot took 66 damage in total, 8 hits, against 77 kills and 26 enemy wind-ups. (g) Living enemies spend about 72% of their time in ENTER or APPROACH against a masher; only about 3% is POSTURE (CROWD: 0.1-0.3 of 5.7 alive posturing). SPEC §7 says 'the danger is numbers'. As built, the danger only lands on a player who does nothing (KO in 15-26 s). The departure 'attacks in turns' (M3-judgement-calls line 97) was measured only against passive or held-back players.

findings.title: The perf act's engine columns are dead or mislabelled: 'bodies' is always 0 under Jolt, and 'process' and 'physics' are per-second maxima, not the last frame
findings.detail: The 'Perf, six with ragdolls' act logs `Performance.PHYSICS_3D_ACTIVE_OBJECTS` as 'the active physics bodies (the ragdolls' bodies count)' (crowd_acts.gd:243, 255). Godot's Jolt server does not report this monitor: it reads 0 even with 5 falling rigid bodies. So every PERF line says '0 bodies' while 26 bodies go down per run, and the act gives no evidence about ragdoll body load. Its doc (crowd_acts.gd:169-171) also calls the 'process' and 'physics' columns 'the engine's own monitors for the last frame'. In Godot 4 these monitors hold the maximum over the last second, and the physics figure sums every tick of a frame. That is why window 1 reads 'physics 93.1' (and 98.5) while the same window's worst wall frame is 23.3 ms (22.0). Both columns mislead anyone citing the act for L6. P4-int's call 20 already says the frame lines are the measure; the instrument's own text says otherwise.
